summary.headline: The Library Board of Trustees agreed to keep the library open Labor Day weekend Saturday and reviewed proposed policy revisions for mobile hotspot lending.
summary.summary: The Southborough Library Board of Trustees reviewed facility maintenance projects, including upcoming LED lighting retrofits and annual carpet cleaning. Trustees debated holiday closure schedules and visitor attendance data, deciding to stay open the Saturday of Labor Day weekend while deferring action on the Saturday after Thanksgiving. The board also received updates on Community Preservation Committee signage recognizing CPA funding, addressed a payroll timing anomaly in the monthly budget report, and previewed policy revisions to penalize mobile hotspot lending violations.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The trustees approved minutes from their June 16, 2026 joint meeting with the Select Board and their regular meeting on July 20, 2026. A trustee clarified an absence and noted a spelling correction needed on the Select Board's draft record.
key_details: Approved minutes from the June 16, 2026 joint meeting with the Select Board
Approved minutes from the July 20, 2026 regular board meeting
Noted a spelling correction for Trustee Ekberg's name on Select Board records

topics.title: Facilities updates and LED lighting retrofit
topics.summary: The library director updated the board on several ongoing facility maintenance projects. An LED lighting conversion is scheduled to begin in August, and the director is coordinating with facilities staff to explore energy-efficient motion-sensor lighting in book stack aisles. Annual carpet cleaning was also scheduled for a Saturday when the building is closed to the public.
key_details: Annual carpet cleaning scheduled for Saturday, August 15 while the library is closed
LED conversion contractor expected to start work during August
Exploring motion-sensor stack lighting to reduce energy consumption
Contractor work scheduled early in mornings to minimize disruption to patrons
Children's room lighting was previously upgraded to LED following flood repairs
topics.outcome: Discussion only; work scheduled for August

topics.title: Holiday closures and Saturday operating schedule
topics.summary: Trustees debated the holiday operating calendar, focusing on whether to close on Saturdays following major holidays. The director presented circulation and door-count data showing that attendance on Saturdays following holidays drops below 25 percent of normal volume, while town personnel rules create complex compensatory time obligations for staff working those weekends. Following discussion, the board agreed to remain open on the Saturday of Labor Day weekend and revisit Thanksgiving weekend staffing next month.
key_details: Door counts show visitor traffic drops below 25 percent of average on holiday weekend Saturdays
Town Salary Administration Plan grants Friday holidays, creating compensatory time challenges for Saturday staff
Trustees agreed the library will remain open on Saturday, September 5 for Labor Day weekend
Early closures planned at 2:00 p.m. on September 21 for staff training, and 5:00 p.m. on Thanksgiving Eve and New Year's Eve
Trustees will evaluate part-time staff availability for the Saturday after Thanksgiving at the September meeting
topics.outcome: Agreement to open Saturday of Labor Day weekend; further review of post-Thanksgiving Saturday set for September

topics.title: Annual state statistical report
topics.summary: The director reported that the library's annual state statistical report has been completed and filed. Overall library utilization and physical circulation remained steady, with digital circulation seeing the largest gains.
key_details: Annual Report Information Survey (ARIS) successfully completed and submitted to the state
Electronic media borrowing through Libby and Hoopla saw the highest rate of growth
Overall circulation and visitor numbers remained stable compared to the prior year

topics.title: FY24 monthly expense report
topics.summary: A trustee flagged that the salary line appeared 16.5 percent over budget in the initial monthly expense report. The director clarified that the reporting period encompassed three biweekly payrolls rather than two, temporarily inflating the expenditure figure.
key_details: Salary expenditure showed 16.5 percent over projected monthly rate
Anomaly was caused by three payroll cycles falling into the first reporting period
Director will monitor staffing costs following two recent employee promotions

topics.title: Community Preservation Committee signage
topics.summary: Trustees received a report on a recent Community Preservation Committee meeting concerning plaques recognizing CPA-funded library projects. The CPC voted to adopt the trustees' preferred language crediting Southborough residents rather than taxpayers or citizens. The signs will display the town seal instead of the library logo, and invoices have been submitted to the CPC for payment.
key_details: CPC agreed to use the term 'residents' on recognition plaques per trustee request
Signs will feature the official town seal at the top rather than the library logo
Signs have been commissioned and invoices forwarded to the CPC
Discussion noted that an existing plaque near the front stairs already recognizes a 2013 facade and stair project
topics.outcome: Signage commissioned; invoices submitted to CPC for reimbursement

topics.title: Mobile hotspot lending policy update
topics.summary: The director previewed upcoming revisions to the library's mobile hotspot lending policy following several compliance issues. Recent problems included an unreturned power charger resulting in a $15 replacement charge and a patron improperly dropping a hotspot into the exterior mailbox on a weekend. Proposed policy changes will explicitly prohibit mailbox returns and establish a six-month borrowing suspension for policy violations.
key_details: A patron was billed a $15 fee to cover the replacement cost of an unreturned charger
A hotspot was improperly deposited in the outdoor mailbox on a Saturday while the library was closed
Proposed policy revisions will establish a six-month suspension of hotspot borrowing for violations
Revisions will clearly prohibit returning electronic equipment in the book drop or mailbox
Formal vote on the updated policy is planned for the September meeting
topics.outcome: Discussion only; revised policy scheduled for board review in September

upcoming.what: Next regular Library Board of Trustees meeting
Early library closure at 2:00 p.m. for staff Dementia Friends training
Board review and vote on revised mobile hotspot lending policy
